newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 30.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Wednesday:
* Employee compensation costs rose slightly this spring because of an increase in benefits, but the gain posed no inflationary threat.
* When Loehmann's Inc went public last year its stock enjoyed a strong run on wall street, only to taper off beginning in April when the company warned of lower-than-expected earnings.

* Tenet HealthCare agreed to pay about $100 million to former patients who contended that the company and some affiliated doctors illegally imprisioned them in psychiatric hospitals in order to obtain their insurance benefits.
* Ford Motor Co announced plans to rejuvenate its tired Mercury division by reviving the Mercury Cougar.
* Stocks reached new highs, buoyed by economic reports that pointed toward low inflation and moderate growth.

* Airtouch Communications' purchase of U.S. West Media Group's United States wireless business will have to be restructured because Congress would not change the date that an adverse provision of the new tax bill takes effect.
* T.I.A.A.-C.R.E.F., the retirement system that serves many of the nation's college professors and administrators, lost its battle to retain its tax-exempt status.
* McDonald's selected the Chicago office of DDB Needham Worldwide as its lead domestic advertising agency.
* Shares in the disk maker Nimbus CD International rose 14 percent after the company announced that it had signed a contract to become an authorized maker of digital disks for Microsoft.
* Bear Stearns said its quarterly earnings were almost unchanged.
